slides.title: Evaluating Generative Agents with Actions Grounded in Socially Distributed Task Environments using Incognita
slides.tldr: EVALUATING GENERATIVE AGENTS IN SOCIALLY DISTRIBUTED TASK ENVIRONMENTS
slides.highlight: The Incognita framework evaluates generative agents' ability to elicit knowledge and execute grounded actions in multi-entity environments, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: Incognita evaluates generative agents in social environments where knowledge is distributed across role-isolated participants.
card.key_idea: A framework separating social interaction from grounded execution, using specialists to mediate operations and a deterministic sub-environment to execute actions over a canonical state.
card.evaluation: Three models tested on 18 Incognita-Retail tasks (540 trials). Success rose from 0% to 17.2%, though overall reliability remains low.
card.limitation: Reliability of agent success remains low despite improvements in knowledge elicitation and grounded action attempts.

slides.title: Will Scaling Improve Social Simulation with LLMs?
slides.tldr: SCALING LAWS IN LLM SOCIAL SIMULATIONS
slides.highlight: This research examines how compute scaling affects the fidelity of LLM-based social simulations, which is relevant to MIMIC's use of LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: Scaling compute generally improves LLM social simulation, but fails for specific cognitive biases and underrepresented populations.
card.key_idea: The authors analyzed compute and observational scaling laws across 120+ models to correlate general capabilities with opinion, behavioral, and longitudinal simulation fidelity.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using WVS, Psych-101, and ACL datasets across 85 controlled Qwen3 models and 35 open-weight models up to 70B parameters.
card.limitation: Scaling fails to improve calibration for human cognitive biases, risk aversion, and populations underrepresented in English web corpora.

slides.title: Designing Touch for Trauma-Informed Social Robots: A Design Space for Direct and Indirect Actuation
slides.tldr: TRAUMA-INFORMED TOUCH DESIGN FOR SOCIAL ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a design space for direct and indirect touch actuation in social robots aligned with trauma-informed care, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A conceptual design space for creating trauma-informed touch interactions in social robots for PTSD support.
card.key_idea: Distinguishes direct and indirect touch across three dimensions: actuation modality, objective (whole/external/internal body), and intended effect (informational, functional, or affective), aligned with trauma-informed care principles.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper provides a conceptual framework and analysis rather than empirical testing or datasets.
card.limitation: The design space is exploratory and has not been empirically evaluated with PTSD patients, therapists, or other stakeholders.

slides.title: TurnNat: Automatic Evaluation of Turn-Taking Naturalness in Dyadic Spoken Dialogue
slides.highlight: TurnNat introduces a likelihood-based framework to automatically evaluate turn-taking naturalness in dyadic dialogue, supporting HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: TurnNat automatically evaluates turn-taking naturalness in dyadic dialogue using future voice-activity likelihoods.
card.key_idea: A causal prediction model estimates future two-speaker voice-activity states; negative log-likelihoods are aggregated over turn-taking boundary units to score dialogue-level naturalness.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a human-validated paired perturbation benchmark (1,000 pairs). Best model (D4) achieved 88.0% matched-pair accuracy and 0.676 C-index.
card.limitation: Focuses on voice activity, potentially missing naturalness cues from lexical content, discourse intent, prosody, or human-AI specific dynamics.

slides.title: From Technical Metrics to User Perception: A User Study of a Multimodal Human-Robot Interaction System for Object Detection and Grasping
slides.tldr: USER PERCEPTION OF MULTIMODAL HRI IMPROVEMENTS
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that technical gains in task success for object-grasping systems are perceptible to users, supporting the need for user-centered evidence in HRI. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied AI.

card.one_liner: A user study confirms that a 15% technical success gain in a robot grasping system is perceptible.
card.key_idea: Compared a baseline HRI system (Florence-2, LLaMA 3.1) against an improved version (Grounding DINO+SAM, Qwen 3.5 9B) using a within-subject user study on tabletop grasping.
card.evaluation: 24 participants rated speed, reliability, and competence on 7-point Likert scales. Results showed significant preference and higher ratings for the improved system (p < 0.05).
card.limitation: Despite improvements, reliability ratings remained near the scale midpoint, indicating the system is not yet fully dependable for real-world deployment.

slides.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Decision-Making in Agent-Based Urban Mobility Simulations
slides.tldr: LLM-BASED DECISION LAYERS FOR URBAN MOBILITY AGENTS
slides.highlight: This research explores using LLMs as cognitive layers in multi-agent simulations to improve adaptability and decision-making in urban mobility, aligning with MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: LLMs improve agent adaptability and arrival rates in urban mobility simulations compared to rule-based heuristics.
card.key_idea: A hybrid architecture connecting the GAMA platform to an LLM-based module (Agno) that decides whether to trigger route recalculation using contextual data and persistent semantic memory.
card.evaluation: Compared rule-based baselines against Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite and GPT-4o Mini across localized/extended blockage scenarios with 500-1000 agents; measured arrival rates and congestion.
card.limitation: Substantial increase in computational overhead and simulation time compared to deterministic rule-based models.

slides.title: SenseWalk: Agent-Based Semantic Trajectory Simulation Powered by Large Language Models in Zoned Environments
slides.highlight: This work introduces SenseWalk, which uses LLM-powered agents and the social force model to simulate human movement and semantic trajectories, aligning with MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: SenseWalk is an interactive system using LLM-powered agents to simulate physically plausible and semantically coherent human trajectories.
card.key_idea: A hybrid workflow combining LLMs for high-level semantic planning and reasoning with a social force model for physically realistic, collision-free movement.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via quantitative experiments across four real-world venue models (physical/semantic loss) and a user study with 12 participants.

slides.title: DuplexChat: Constructing Speaker-Separated Full-Duplex Dialogue Speech at Scale for Spoken Dialogue Language Modeling
slides.highlight: This work introduces DuplexChat and a pipeline to create speaker-separated dialogue speech, supporting HyECHO's focus on diarization and multimodal social perception of human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: DuplexChat provides a scalable pipeline and large corpus of speaker-separated full-duplex dialogue speech from podcasts.
card.key_idea: DuplexChat-Pipe uses RSS feed filtering, diarization-based segmentation, and the DialogueSidon diffusion model to convert monaural podcast audio into separate audio tracks for two speakers.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using DNSMOS, STOI, PESQ, ITC, and ITD against the Fisher corpus; results show competitive acoustic quality and natural turn-taking dynamics.
card.limitation: Japanese speaker separation quality is lower than English, likely due to limited Japanese training data for the DialogueSidon model.

slides.title: NormWorlds-CF: Solver-Verified Counterfactual Normative Reasoning with Metamorphic-Relation GRPO
slides.highlight: Introduces a solver-verified environment and MR-GRPO to improve counterfactual normative reasoning in LLMs, supporting MIMIC's use of LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: NormWorlds-CF uses solver-verified counterfactuals and MR-GRPO to improve structural normative reasoning beyond final-answer accuracy.
card.key_idea: A solver-verified environment providing deterministic certificates and a class-conditioned GRPO reward (MR-GRPO) that gives partial credit for metamorphic relation families and structural change fields.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via staged SFT diagnostics and matched GRPO experiments (1.7B and 4B models) using deterministic solvers on ID and OOD test splits.
card.limitation: Exact full change-record generation, invariant subtype recognition, and out-of-distribution (OOD) transfer remain open challenges.

slides.title: C³ASD: Multi-Level Consistency-Driven Representation Learning
slides.highlight: This work proposes a consistency-driven framework for Active Speaker Detection that improves robustness against real-world corruptions, supporting HyECHO's goals in multimodal social perception and identity recognition.

card.one_liner: C³ASD improves Active Speaker Detection robustness against real-world audio-visual corruptions using multi-level consistency regularization.
card.key_idea: Three complementary constraints: embedding-level inter-modality alignment during speech, track-aware intra-modality contrastive learning for cluster separation, and prediction-level knowledge distillation from multimodal to unimodal streams.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on AVA-ActiveSpeaker and WASD datasets, plus MUSAN/DEMAND noise and visual occlusions. Results show improved mAP, especially under joint corruptions.

slides.title: HABIT: Human-Aware Behavior and Interaction Training Dataset for Robot Manipulation
slides.highlight: HABIT provides a large-scale dataset of robot demonstrations in human-present environments, enabling policies to learn spatiotemporal synchronization, yielding, and gesture grounding. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: HABIT is a large-scale robot demonstration dataset designed to teach robots human-aware behaviors in shared workspaces.
card.key_idea: 10K+ episodes across 60 tasks categorized into three interaction roles: Collaborator (joint goals), Coworker (shared space), and Supervisor (human-directed cues).
card.evaluation: Fine-tuned $\pi_{0.5}$ and GR00T N1.6 models; compared against robot-only baselines using success rates, workflow compliance, and safety metrics across six representative tasks.
card.limitation: Collected in a single environment with ten operators, limiting diversity in body silhouettes, motion styles, and multi-agent dynamics.
